(1) leukocytes can enter the CNS parenchyma via the perivascular space, (2) the glia limitens can be breached by leukocytes, (3) this breach is mediated in part by MMP-9, and (4) the breach can be prevented by blocking MMP-9.
leukocytes recruited into the brain parenchyma require two differentially regulated processes to traverse the BBB, and that the second step involves antigen recognition and induction of MMPs.

(i) leukocyte entry into the central nervous system is a two-step process, (ii) leukocyte recruitment across the glia-limitans is a highly selective process that is regulated by the presence of specific adhesion molecules and their ligands, and (iii) the glia limitants acts as an enzymatic barrier that can be modified by the presence of leukocyte-derived MMPs.
